documents.title: Current public mandate
documents.text: Ragunauth “Randy” Ramsaroop serves as Liaison Director in the Social Responsibility Department at Aurora Gold Mines Inc. His consolidated tenure with AGM dates from 2020.

documents.title: Professional focus
documents.text: His professional focus spans ESG and social responsibility, corporate affairs, government relations, compliance, stakeholder engagement, public relations, aviation coordination and dispatch-related interfaces in a natural-resources operating environment.

documents.title: Government and institutional interfaces
documents.text: His work has involved engagement across Guyanese public institutions and regulators including mining, environmental, energy, aviation, police, standards, revenue, gold, natural-resources, labour, investment and other government interfaces.

documents.title: ESG and social responsibility
documents.text: The public professional record positions him at the intersection of ESG, social responsibility, stakeholder relationships, institutional trust and responsible growth in mining and natural resources.

documents.title: Corporate affairs approach
documents.text: The corporate-affairs approach presented on the site emphasises aligning operating priorities with institutions, public expectations, evidence, internal decision-making and follow-through rather than treating external affairs as a stand-alone communications function.

documents.title: Government relations approach
documents.text: His published perspective frames government relations as disciplined institutional engagement: understand legal mandates, distinguish facts from requests, prepare evidence, respect decision authority, document commitments and follow through.

documents.title: Responsible mining perspective
documents.text: His mining-related work and writing focus on responsible operations, stakeholder trust, community relationships, regulatory complexity, local capability, ESG credibility and the connection between institutional performance and operating execution.

documents.title: Energy and transition perspective
documents.text: His public work on energy and natural resources examines reliability, renewable transition, industrial demand, diesel displacement, energy security and the institutional conditions required for responsible growth.

documents.title: Professional development
documents.text: His professional development includes Zijin Mining Group headquarters training in 2023 and participation in a Management Reserve Program in 2023.

documents.title: Internal recognition
documents.text: His record includes a Best of Best Second Merit Award received in 2021.

documents.title: External sustainability recognition
documents.text: Aurora Gold Mines Inc. received external recognition in 2026 including ECONOME Employer of the Year and an International Sustainability Award connected with its renewable-energy and climate-resilience work.

documents.title: International energy recognition
documents.text: Aurora Gold Mines Inc. was selected as a 2026 SAEEC Energy Awards finalist in the Industrial Energy Project of the Year category.

documents.title: Public speaking
documents.text: His public speaking themes include responsible mining, nation-building, ESG, energy transition, corporate affairs, institutional trust and the role of natural-resource organisations in long-term development.

documents.title: Evidence standard
documents.text: The site uses an evidence-led standard for professional claims: distinguish direct ownership from contribution, quantify only verified outcomes, explain methods and controls, and avoid inflated attribution.

documents.title: Executive positioning
documents.text: The public profile is positioned for senior responsibilities across ESG, corporate affairs, government relations, external affairs, social performance and country-level natural-resources leadership.

documents.title: Stakeholder trust
documents.text: The case-study framing emphasises the operating value of stakeholder trust, structured engagement, clear accountability, issue escalation and documented follow-through.

documents.title: Governance and compliance
documents.text: The governance perspective on the site stresses evidence, accountability, delegated authority, regulatory discipline, issue ownership and controls that withstand scrutiny.

documents.title: Guyana context
documents.text: His professional and research work is grounded in Guyana while addressing international natural-resources, energy, ESG and institutional questions.

documents.title: The Physical Limits of Artificial Intelligence
documents.text: Research on electricity, grids, water, cooling, chips, critical minerals, finance, cybersecurity and the physical infrastructure requirements of advanced artificial intelligence through 2035.

documents.title: From Ore to Optionality
documents.text: A flagship study of critical-mineral partnerships, value addition, industrial capability, supply-chain resilience, ESG, finance and strategic optionality.

documents.title: Fresh Water: The Next Strategic Commodity
documents.text: An assessment of dependable freshwater access as a strategic constraint across economic growth, food systems, industry, technology, infrastructure and capital allocation.

documents.title: Critical Minerals Are the New Energy Security
documents.text: Research on strategic mineral supply, processing concentration, trade controls, investment, ESG, industrial policy and resilience across critical mineral value chains.

documents.title: Guyana 2040: From Resource Wealth to Strategic Statecraft
documents.text: A framework for translating Guyana's resource wealth into enduring institutional, productive, financial, human, natural and national capabilities.

documents.title: Guyana Power Demand 2030
documents.text: An evidence-led assessment separating measured electricity demand from development scenarios and examining generation, grid and reliability requirements through 2030.

documents.title: Beyond Employment: Enterprise Stewardship and the Ownership Orientation of Executive Leadership
documents.text: A multidisciplinary paper on stewardship, governance, enterprise risk, culture, stakeholder value, executive decision-making and long-horizon performance.

documents.title: Karpowership Guyana 2026-2035
documents.text: Independent public-data analysis of a possible transition from bridge generation toward flexible reliability and strategic energy infrastructure in Guyana.

documents.title: Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and the 2026 UN Secretary-General Selection
documents.text: Independent public-record analysis of candidacy context, United Nations selection architecture and documented leadership considerations related to the 2026 Secretary-General process.

documents.title: The Geopolitics of Gold
documents.text: Analysis of central banks, reserve diversification, monetary resilience, responsible sourcing and the strategic role of gold in changing geopolitical and financial conditions.

documents.title: Guyana Development Bank
documents.text: Independent policy analysis of productive finance, SME participation, governance, additionality and measurable development outcomes in Guyana.

documents.title: The New Geography of Globalization
documents.text: A comparative study of trade, industrial policy, investment, technology, supply-chain restructuring and strategic dependence during geopolitical fragmentation.

documents.title: Guyana Economy 2030
documents.text: An academic and executive research monograph on the choices, assumptions and risks involved in converting exceptional resource revenue into durable national prosperity.

documents.title: Water Security as Economic Security
documents.text: A systems analysis of water risk across agriculture, energy, industry, AI infrastructure, finance, trade, cities and national resilience.

documents.title: Sovereign AI: Who Controls the Intelligence Infrastructure?
documents.text: A systems-level study of authority, continuity, substitutability and assurance across compute, cloud, chips, data and institutional capability.

documents.title: The Trust Deficit
documents.text: Research on warranted institutional trust as an operating condition for cooperation, reform, resilience, transformation and execution capacity.

documents.title: Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030
documents.text: An independent evidence review of forest conservation, carbon finance, national development and governance accountability under Guyana's Low Carbon Development Strategy 2030.

documents.title: Guyana's Forest Carbon Economy
documents.text: Independent research into Guyana's jurisdictional forest-carbon programme, accounting integrity, commercial agreements, revenue governance and long-term climate accountability.

documents.title: Guyana's Global Biodiversity Alliance
documents.text: Independent research into biodiversity governance, nature finance, biodiversity measurement, Indigenous participation, data architecture and 30x30 implementation questions.

documents.title: Who Pays for the Energy Transition?
documents.text: A decision framework for assessing who finances energy-transition infrastructure, who carries risk and how to evaluate affordability, reliability, fiscal durability and public outcomes.

documents.title: Omai Gold 2026 PEA: From Preliminary Economics to Verifiable Development Readiness
documents.text: Independent technical, financial and environmental review of Omai Gold's August 2026 preliminary economic assessment, with attention to assumptions, development readiness and ESG considerations.
